Beyond the visible lesion: mycotoxin attenuation and spatial heterogeneity in maize cobs
nodes.venue: Mycotoxin Research
nodes.abstract: Abstract Visible mould is widely used as a practical sorting cue in maize, but it remains unclear whether the visible lesion marks the boundary of mycotoxin contamination within an intact cob. This study examined mycotoxin attenuation, spatial heterogeneity, and co-occurrence in visibly mouldy white maize cobs, using measured distances from the visible mould margin. Cobs with visible mould ( n = 35) were sampled for the study. For each cob, the visible mould margin was coded as 0 mm, and adjacent sections were collected at the 50% and 75% points along the measured distance from the lesion boundary to the distal cob tip, resulting in 98 cob-section observations. Mycotoxins, FUMs (FB1, FB2, FB3), deoxynivalenol (DON), zearalenone (ZEA), nivalenol (NIV) and AF (AFB1) were quantified by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. Samples with no detectable levels of mycotoxins were replaced with zero, and total FUMs were calculated (FB1 + FB2 + FB3). The visible mould margin accounted for the largest share of the measured toxin burden, accounting for 84.4% of total FUM, 89.4% of DON, 77.8% of ZEA, and 92.2% of NIV. Adjacent sections retained measurable residual mycotoxins, including 15.6% of total FUM, 10.6% of DON, 22.2% of ZEA, and 7.8% of NIV. In full-distance models, DON, ZEA, and NIV declined significantly with distance, whereas total FUM did not show significant monotonic attenuation. The AFB1 was detected in only three cob sections; these detections co-occurred with Fusarium -associated toxins. Co-occurrence analysis showed that adjacent sections frequently remained positive for multiple Fusarium -associated toxin groups, with the FUM + DON + ZEA profile persisting across measured-distance bands. These findings show that visible mould is a useful warning signal but not a reliable toxicological boundary. The results support cob-level rejection or segregation of visibly mouldy cobs before shelling, rather than lesion-level trimming, as a more defensible food-safety control measure.

nodes.name: Breaking GUI Agent Actions: Realistic Adversarial Attacks on Multimodal LLMs
nodes.venue: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
nodes.abstract: Recent progress in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has enabled GUI agents that interpret interface screenshots and execute natural-language instructions. However, their increasing role in human–computer interaction raises security concerns. Existing work shows that MLLMs are highly sensitive to interface perturbations, yet most attacks assume unrealistic capabilities such as direct access to model-ready inputs. In real deployments, attackers cannot control the screenshot pipeline or the non-differentiable preprocessing operations preceding inference, rendering many prior attacks ineffective. We introduce Realistic Adversarial Attack (RAA) framework that models the complete screenshot-to-prediction pipeline. To address gradient blockage from non-differentiable preprocessing (e.g., resizing and quantization), we develop a dual-branch differentiable preprocessing module that restores gradient flow while remaining faithful to the actual inference path. To improve robustness against query phrasing changes, we further incorporate a task-level semantic variation mechanism that jointly optimizes over paraphrased task variants. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B-Instruct and GUI-Owl-7B show that RAA consistently outperforms prior attacks, improving attack success rates by an average of 30% under localized perturbations and a 10.7% under global perturbations, while maintaining strong effectiveness against standard defenses such as resizing, compression, and noise. Ablation studies highlight the roles of perturbation region and semantic diversity. Our framework establishes a practical threat model for GUI agents and offers a foundation for future robustness and security research.

nodes.name: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
A Physics‐Informed Two‐Stage Retrieval Method for EMIT Remote Sensing Methane Plumes
nodes.venue: Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres
nodes.abstract: Abstract Hyperspectral satellite missions, particularly EMIT, have revolutionized methane point source monitoring. However, current operational retrieval pipelines typically rely on physically‐based matched filters followed by labor‐intensive manual verification to mitigate high false alarm rates caused by complex background interference. This dependence on human intervention restricts the scalability and efficiency required for rapid, automated global monitoring. To address these limitations, this paper proposes Plume‐Net, a novel Physics‐Informed Guided Two‐Stage Retrieval Method. Unlike conventional approaches, Plume‐Net decouples the task into a “global existence classification” stage and a “local pixel‐level regression” stage to maximize reliability without human‐in‐the‐loop. The core innovation lies in the integration of physical priors with deep learning: In the first stage, a Physics‐Informed Spectral Gating (PISG) module explicitly injects methane spectral absorption knowledge into the network, dynamically recalibrating channel weights to suppress background noise. In the second stage, to overcome the difficulties of regressing sparse, long‐tail plume distributions, we propose a Plume‐Focused Sampling Strategy and an Intensity‐Aware Pixel‐Level Weighted Loss function, forcing the network to prioritize rare but critical high‐concentration signals. Evaluated on real‐world EMIT observations, Plume‐Net achieves an ROC‐AUC of 0.961 in detection and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 33.33 ppm·m in quantification. By significantly reducing false positives while maintaining high precision, this method offers a robust, fully automated alternative to current semi‐manual retrieval workflows.

nodes.name: Warming up ground-state orbitals: A route to excitation energies?
nodes.venue: The Journal of Chemical Physics
nodes.abstract: Linear-response time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) is the workhorse of spectral prediction, yet it can struggle to predict or even describe important low-lying excitation energies. An alternative is to use static formalisms to target excited-state energies directly from variational density functional theory (DFT). This may involve using custom excited-state functionals or feeding excited-state orbitals and densities into standard ground-state approximations, and can often be effective, even for describing states for which adiabatic TDDFT fails. However, this comes at the cost of requiring specialized algorithms to find stationary points. In this exploratory work, we demonstrate that finite-temperature DFT can provide an effective auxiliary framework for generating excited-state-like orbitals from ground-state orbitals for modern ensemble and state-specific functionals, such as the GX24 ground-state (G) and excited-state (X) functional. Notably, the necessary fixed-point algorithms are already available and well optimized in many electronic-structure codes.

nodes.name: Artificial intelligence in food safety: a bibliometric and empirical synthesis of emerging technologies and research frontiers
nodes.venue: British Food Journal
nodes.abstract: Purpose This study aimed to identify recent research trends in the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with food safety and security through a comprehensive bibliometric analysis. Design/methodology/approach A total of 2,782 documents published between 2021 and 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. The dataset was refined by removing duplicates, filtering document types and excluding irrelevant records. VOSviewer was then used to conduct co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, citation, co-citation and bibliographic coupling analyses. Findings Machine learning and deep learning emerged as core technologies associated with food security, contamination detection and quality prediction. Keyword clustering demonstrated interdisciplinary connections with agriculture, climate change and public health. Citation and co-citation analyses identified three major intellectual foundations: traditional machine learning, computer vision-based deep learning and time-series modeling. China, India and the United States were the most influential contributors in terms of research output and technological development. Bibliographic coupling and source co-citation analyses further indicated increasing convergence between food science and computational science. Originality/value This study provides a comprehensive overview of the intellectual structure, collaborative networks and thematic evolution of AI-driven food safety research. Unlike previous studies focusing on specific technologies or applications, it maps global research patterns and interdisciplinary linkages. The findings provide strategic insights for researchers, policymakers and industry stakeholders. Future studies should prioritize explainable AI integration into regulatory frameworks and the development of larger, more diverse datasets to improve model generalizability across food systems.

nodes.name: Lightweight event recognition framework for Φ-OTDR systems with space-frequency fusion based on self-exclusion relational knowledge distillation
nodes.venue: Applied Optics
nodes.abstract: Phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (Φ-OTDR) systems are widely utilized in large-scale perimeter security and critical infrastructure protection. However, disturbance signal classification in Φ-OTDR systems heavily relies on complex model structures. Achieving high classification accuracy often requires high computational demands and substantial costs. This paper proposes an ultra-lightweight classification framework named space-frequency self-exclusion relational knowledge distillation (SF-SERKD). This framework constructs a three-channel feature map by using the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) combined with gradient analysis to capture the frequency-domain and spatial mutation features of signals. In addition, the framework introduces an innovative self-exclusion relational knowledge distillation (SERKD) strategy, which explicitly excludes the target sample’s own teacher features during the nearest-neighbor matching process. This strategy forces the student model to abandon feature alignment with high-noise samples or isolated samples, thereby reconstructing a robust and shared intra-class feature structure. Validation results in two different scenarios show that the student model achieves classification accuracies of 99.81% and 99.29%, alongside ultra-low nuisance alarm rates of 0.0004 and 0.0037, respectively, while only requiring 0.007M parameters. Notably, the accuracy of the student model in the second scenario is 1.87% higher than that of the teacher network. These results elucidate the effectiveness and generalization of the proposed method for real-time vibration event recognition in Φ-OTDR systems.

nodes.name: Spatial Super-Resolution of Satellite-Derived SST Data via Generative Adversarial Networks in the Mediterranean Sea
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: In this work, we compare deep convolutional and generative models to improve the reconstruction of sea surface temperature (SST) gradients and effective resolution from cloud-contaminated satellite infrared data. Standard gap-filling techniques produce spatially complete datasets, but they inherently smooth out fine-scale features and gradients that may be critical for a better understanding of the ocean dynamics. Here, we investigate how the use of deep learning models as Autoencoders (AEs) and generative models as Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (C-GANs) differently contribute to recovering the small-scale structures lost during interpolation. Our supervised, observation-based training relies on satellite-derived SST data from the Mediterranean Sea, with a focus on learning the statistical relationship between high-resolution fields and their low-resolution counterparts. We apply a tiling and merging strategy to deal with limited observational coverage and to ensure spatial continuity. Quantitative validation based on mean squared error metrics, spectral analysis, and gradient statistics shows that the AE reduces the reconstruction error, but it fails to recover high-frequency variability. In contrast, the C-GAN effectively restores the statistical properties of the true SST field at the cost of increasing the pointwise discrepancy with the ground truth observations. Our results highlight the potential of deep models to enhance the physical and statistical realism of gap-filled satellite data in oceanographic applications.

nodes.name: Spatial Structure in UAV Visual Geolocalization: Controlled Evaluation of Descriptor Pooling and Geographic Index Partitioning
nodes.abstract: Abstract Absolute visual localization lets a UAV estimate its position without GNSS by matching onboard imagery against a georeferenced map. Two design assumptions are widespread: that encoding where a feature appears improves the descriptor, and that partitioning the index geographically reduces retrieval cost. Direct evidence for either design choice remains limited because comparisons often lack an appropriately matched baseline: descriptor studies can confound spatial structure with patch-token use, while hierarchical indices are seldom evaluated directly against exhaustive search. We evaluate both assumptions using a frozen vision foundation backbone on synthetic queries and 1104 frames from three UAV flights, with end-to-end profiling on an embedded GPU. Neither assumption is supported under the evaluated configuration. Radially structured token pooling, at eight times the dimensionality of a plain global descriptor, is significantly worse on both query sets, and a patch-token mean-pooling control shows that the deficit is not explained by patch-token use alone. Aggregating the query over rotations increases inference time by 3.70 times without improving accuracy. Geographic partitioning increases median error by up to a factor of eight while occupying more memory and running slower on the target device. A 384-dimensional class token in a flat exact index localizes 120 m real-flight frames to a median of 68.7 m; on the edge device, the corresponding pipeline runs at 136 ms per frame, 1.65 J per frame and 12.1 W. Data and code are released.

nodes.name: Satellite-Based Estimation of Monthly Rainfall Across the Indonesian Archipelago: A Month-Specific Multiple Linear Regression Framework Using Bias-Corrected NASA POWER Data over Java, Bali, Nusa Tenggara, and Maluku
nodes.abstract: Abstract Reliable long-term rainfall records remain scarce across Indonesia because the freely accessible BMKG Data Online portal typically distributes only daily observations for roughly the two most recent years, which is insufficient for robust trend analysis and model calibration. This study develops and evaluates a transparent, month-specific Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) framework for estimating monthly rainfall across four Indonesian regions Java, Bali, Nusa Tenggara, and Maluku using bias-corrected NASA Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources (NASA POWER) satellite data (2011–2026) as predictors and BMKG station observations as the reference. Air temperature (T2M), relative humidity (RH2M), and wind speed (WS2M) were used as predictors, and the satellite precipitation field was first bias-corrected against gauge data using a probability-curve (duration-curve) approach. Twelve month-specific regression equations were fitted per region and evaluated at 66 BMKG stations using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), the Pearson correlation coefficient (R), Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE), and Relative Bias (RB). Aggregated regional performance was good in every region: Java (RMSE = 139.18 mm/month, R = 0.65, NSE = 0.50, RB = 5.67%), Bali (183.41, 0.73, 0.70, 3.76%), Nusa Tenggara (148.93, 0.70, 0.63, 5.41%), and Maluku (190.81, 0.64, 0.50, 12.35%). Relative humidity and air temperature were the dominant predictors, whereas wind speed was mostly negative during the dry monsoon. The results confirm that bias-corrected NASA POWER data provide a viable, low-cost alternative for monthly rainfall estimation in data-sparse regions of central and eastern Indonesia, supporting water-resource planning, hydrometeorological disaster mitigation, and evidence-based public policy.

nodes.name: Revealing the Hidden Archaeological Landscape of Ancient Colchis Using Multispectral and Thermal UAV Remote Sensing
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: This study investigates the potential of integrated multispectral and thermal UAV remote sensing for detecting and mapping hidden archaeological structures of Proto-Colchian and Colchian settlement systems of the 3rd–1st millennium BCE, within the Rioni River basin in western Georgia. Characteristic settlement mounds (Dikhagudzuba), moats/ditches, and possible paleochannel networks represent a unique example of large-scale adaptation to waterlogged environments, and limited archaeological excavations have significantly hindered the identification and interpretation of these buried landscape features. Pilot UAV surveys were conducted at four archaeological sites differing in location, geomorphological setting, land use, and degree of preservation using DJI Mavic 3M multispectral and DJI Matrice 4T thermal UAV platforms. Multispectral imagery enabled the detection of vegetation and soil-moisture anomalies associated with buried ditches, embankments, canals, and settlement structures, while thermal data revealed differences in thermal inertia related to subsurface archaeological remains and palaeohydrological features. The study covered approximately 15.4 ha and produced 5836 RGB, 2219 multispectral, and 3617 thermal images with spatial resolutions ranging from 1.87 to 4.61 cm. The integration of high-resolution elevation models, RGB imagery, vegetation indices (ExG and normalized EVI2), and thermal data enabled the identification and characterization of microtopographic, vegetation, moisture, and thermal anomalies associated with archaeological and palaeohydrological features. The investigated mounds cover 2754–4685 m2, reach approximately 9–10 m in height, and are surrounded by moats/ditches covering 4265–6520 m2 and ramparts reaching approximately 2–3.5 m in height. The results demonstrate that combined UAV-based multispectral and thermal remote sensing provides a highly effective non-invasive tool for archaeological prospection in dynamic wetland landscapes. The proposed approach significantly improves the detection of buried archaeological features and paleochannels, while also supporting landscape-scale analyses, monitoring of archaeological heritage, and the development of predictive archaeological models for western Georgia.

nodes.name: QASHI: Quality-Aware Scale-Protected Hybrid Inference for Small-Object Detection in Optical and SAR Remote Sensing Imagery
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Object detection in high-resolution remote sensing imagery faces a resolution–context trade-off: resizing weakens small objects, whereas cropping can truncate targets and remove context. We present QASHI, a detector-retraining-free hybrid inference framework combining a full-image view, four overlapping tiles, and at most three additional regions of interest (ROIs). Quality-Aware Density (QAD) prioritizes local re-inference by combining small-candidate density with weak responses, candidate competition, and full/tile prediction inconsistency. Graph-based ranking correction, bounded BoxVote refinement, and scale-protected routing integrate local predictions with full-image context. Experiments cover VisDrone2019-DET, DIOR, SeaDronesSee v2, and SRSDD-v1.0 with two RT-DETR detectors. On VisDrone-val with RT-DETRv4-S, QASHI improves AP by 2.84 points over the SAHI baseline while reducing mean latency by 14.40%. Relative to Full, it gains 5.74 AP points at 4.52 times the latency. Selector ablations and local parameter analyses characterize how region priority and fusion settings affect detection accuracy and computational cost. On SRSDD, display-domain image-quality sensitivity tests with RT-DETR-R50 yield higher mean perturbed AP (32.52 versus 31.41), with relative AP retention of 93.44% versus 93.98%. QASHI combines prediction-guided local processing and source-aware fusion to improve remote sensing detection through inference-time use of a fixed detector.

nodes.name: PI-Unet Rapid Prediction Method for Satellite Transient Temperature Fields Based on Filtering Concept
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract: To address the low computational efficiency problem by numerical calculation and large cumulative error by long-term sequential iterative prediction during the process of predicting the satellite’s transient temperature fields, this paper proposes a Physics-Informed U-Net (PI-Unet) model. Specifically, this PI-Unet model uses multi-branch spatiotemporal features as its inputs and combines hard constraints with a physics-informed loss to ensure the physical consistency of the predicted temperature field. Furthermore, for the error accumulation problem in long-sequence autoregressive prediction models, this paper presents a model training method based on the concept of filtering. Under the guidance of this method, the PI-Unet model can develop a long-term sequence prediction capability while keeping the accuracy of spatial temperature field prediction, achieving high-precision spatiotemporal prediction. By actively injecting prediction errors through a scheduled sampling strategy, along with a multi-step rolling training strategy, the PI-Unet model not only learns the governing physical laws of the spatial distribution of the transient temperature field, but also acquires the filtering capability to mitigate the accumulation of the long-term sequence rolling prediction errors. The experimental results indicate that the PI-Unet model maintains the maximum absolute error of predicting spatial transient temperature field stably below 5.5K and the error of the rolling-predicted transient temperature field in one orbit period less than 6K. In addition, the time for a single-step prediction is reduced to 0.005s, and the time for a total-period prediction is less than 0.5s. Therefore, this research provides a strong and high-efficiency technical support for the real-time monitoring of the satellite’s on-orbit temperature fields.

nodes.name: OpenClaw-Enabled Real-Time Diagnosis of Inter-Satellite Links in Decentralized Satellite Network Emulation
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract: With the continued expansion of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, inter-satellite links (ISLs) have become a critical infrastructure for network connectivity and end-to-end forwarding capability. Existing studies often show a gap between the physical layer and the system layer: physical factors such as link budget, pointing error, and Doppler mismatch are frequently simplified, while link performance analysis is difficult to validate in a closed loop using a real protocol stack. In addition, dynamic topology and time-varying link states make fault detection and localization highly complex.To address these problems, this paper constructs a decentralized satellite network emulation platform and proposes a decentralized addressing and connectivity verification method for full inter-satellite link interfaces. At the physical layer, an optical inter-satellite link (OISL) model is developed by incorporating free-space path loss, Doppler mismatch, and BER-FEC-PLR mapping, with its dynamic evolution driven by orbital parameters. At the system layer, based on a one-satellite-one-container architecture, OpenClaw is introduced to perform link detection and log analysis, thereby generating diagnostic reports.Experimental results show that the proposed method supports interface-level link detection, identifies dynamic link faults such as transient impairments caused by Doppler mismatch in real time, and generates corresponding diagnostic reports.

nodes.name: Multimodal LLM-based Query Paraphrasing for Video Search
nodes.venue: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
nodes.abstract: Text-to-video retrieval answers user queries through searches based on concepts and embeddings. However, due to limitations in the size of the concept bank and the amount of training data, answering queries in the wild is not always effective because of the out-of-vocabulary problem. Furthermore, neither concept-based nor embedding-based search can perform reasoning to consolidate search results for complex queries that include logical and spatial constraints. To address these challenges, we leverage large language models (LLMs) to paraphrase queries using text-to-text (T2T), text-to-image (T2I), and image-to-text (I2T) transformations. These transformations rephrase abstract concepts into simpler terms to mitigate the out-of-vocabulary problem. Additionally, complex relationships within a query can be decomposed into simpler sub-queries, improving retrieval performance by effectively fusing the search results of these sub-queries. To mitigate the issue of LLM hallucination, this paper also proposes a novel consistency-based verification strategy to filter out factually incorrect paraphrased queries. Extensive experiments are conducted for ad-hoc video search and known-item search on the TRECVid datasets. We provide empirical insights into how traditionally difficult-to-answer queries can be effectively resolved through query paraphrasing.

nodes.name: LLM-Based Satellite Multimodal Knowledge Graph Construction: A Context-Aware Self-Interpretable Paradigm
nodes.venue: SAE technical papers on CD-ROM/SAE technical paper series
nodes.abstract: This paper addresses three main bottlenecks in commercial aerospace multimodal data: semantic alignment difficulties, rigid ontologies, and context loss. We propose a method to construct satellite multimodal knowledge graphs (KGs) using Large Language Model (LLM).The process begins with layout analysis. This step preprocesses interleaved text-image satellite documents to align cross-modal semantics. To resolve ambiguity in technical terms, we developed a triple-positioning entity extraction mechanism. This mechanism directly identifies the original text, summaries, and entity types. For event nodes, we use an event-centric modeling paradigm. This paradigm captures spatio-temporal elements and other meta informations to ensure the nodes are self-interpretable. Entity normalization and automatic schema recognition rely on deep vector embedding. This embedding can semantic clustering the entities for the KG, eliminates the need for prior ontologies. We tested the method on real satellite datasets. The experimental results show high logical integrity and confirm its practical value for aerospace failure analysis.

nodes.name: SAE technical papers on CD-ROM/SAE technical paper series
Invoice layout structure parsing: field mismatch detection model based on visual text joint encoding
nodes.venue: International Conference on Computer Vision, Algorithm, and Image Processing (CVAIP 2026)
nodes.abstract: In order to solve the problems of field value misconnection, detail line misalignment and regional attribution deviation in OCR analysis of invoice images, a field mismatch detection model based on visual text joint coding was proposed. The model firstly divides the invoice layout into regions and extracts field nodes, then fuses visual region features, OCR text semantics and spatial location coding, establishes the field node relationship through cross-modal attention, and uses the content location consistency constraint to output the mismatch confidence. The experiment constructs a data set of 6200 multi-format invoice images, which contains 89460 field nodes and 126800 candidate edges. The test results show that the model achieves Precision 94.2%, Recall 92.6%, F1 93.4%, AUC 96.8%, and mismatching rate 4.7% on 930 test images, which is better than rule matching and single modal model, and verifies the effectiveness of the method in complex layout field relationship detection.

nodes.name: International Conference on Computer Vision, Algorithm, and Image Processing (CVAIP 2026)
Geospatial assessment of Japanese encephalitis virus infection risk in Australia
nodes.abstract: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) is a leading cause of viral encephalitis in humans in Asia. Prior to 2021, only sporadic outbreaks had been detected in Australia's tropical northern extremes. However, during 2021-23, JEV infection was identified in 45 people and in more than 85 piggeries, together with many detections in feral pigs, mosquitoes, and other livestock across Australia, including in the temperate far south. Here we estimated the spatial extent of virus transmission during the outbreak (the realised niche) and the area environmentally suitable for transmission (the potential niche). We collated a national dataset of JEV surveillance and detection in humans, mosquitoes, domestic pigs, feral pigs, and sentinel chickens from 2021-23. We combined these data with (1) previously published predictions of habitat suitability for vertebrate host and vector species, and (2) estimated densities of humans, domestic pigs, and feral pigs, in a multipart assessment of spatial risk. Our model projected broad potential environmental suitability over much of northern and eastern Australia during the outbreak period, but floodplain wetland areas in the north and the inland east of Australia had both the highest estimated environmental suitability for transmission, and the strongest evidence for virus circulation.

nodes.name: Efficient Extrapolation-Based Dynamic Link Prediction for Large-Scale Satellite Networks
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract: Inter-satellite links (ISLs) in large LEO constellations vary quickly with time, and their rapid change makes future link-state prediction a practical concern. Predicting ISLs with reasonable accuracy benefits routing decisions, resource scheduling, and overall network stability. Existing methods are still limited in several ways. Rule-based and physics-based methods build on hand-crafted assumptions, which become unreliable once links flicker frequently or topologies grow heterogeneous. Static graph neural networks describe the relations within a single snapshot, but their formulation does not represent how ISLs evolve from one moment to the next. Many recent dynamic graph models stay close to interpolation, and they exploit physical and temporal satellite attributes only in part, which weakens both node representations and prediction accuracy. To address these gaps, we develop an extrapolation-oriented dynamic link prediction framework with three contributions: (1) we shift the task from interpolation toward future-state extrapolation, which makes proactive management possible; (2) we extract physics- and temporal-aware node features by combining orbital dynamics with historical ISL information; (3) we restrict prediction to a candidate edge set, so the computation stays manageable while the method remains scalable. In experiments, the proposed method outperforms existing baselines on accuracy, efficiency, and scalability, suggesting that it can serve as a useful tool for managing large-scale LEO networks in practice.

nodes.name: Data-based surrogate modeling and performance prediction of MEMS touch mode capacitive sensing using deep multilayer perceptron networks
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Introduction This work presents a structurally optimized rectangular diaphragm that operates in touch mode as the basis for a high-performance micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS) capacitive pressure sensor (CPS). Rectangular diaphragms offer significant advantages in terms of structural control, constant stress handling and directional extension of the contact region. Methods The proposed framework encompasses structural design, analytical modeling, numerical computation, finite element analysis (FEA) and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based prediction. In this design, greater directional control results in a smoother and more reliable change in capacitance with pressure. The rectangular diaphragm design can be changed to smooth the transition between normal and touch modes and produce more consistent linearity and sensitivity. Numerical computation, FEA simulation and deep neural network (DNN) surrogate model for predicting the performance characteristics of a novel MEMS capacitive pressure sensor. A comprehensive dataset is constructed by combining Numerical computation and FEA-simulated results across a wide range of diaphragm geometries and applied pressure conditions. A DNN surrogate model is subsequently developed and trained on this dataset to predict the performance characteristics of the proposed MEMS capacitive pressure sensor. Results The model achieves an overall mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.22 % and R2 above 0.999 across all four outputs, a substantial speed improvement, with prediction time reduced to a matter of seconds compared to the tens of min required for direct FEA simulation. Discussion The results show that the proposed rectangular diaphragm effectively controls the touch region. It also improves capacitance and sensitivity. The DNN surrogate model predicts sensor performance precisely and efficiently. It enables rapid design-space exploration for MEMS capacitive pressure sensors.

nodes.name: DMFNet: Phase-Enhanced Multi-Level Deformable Fusion for Multimodal Remote Sensing Classification
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: The collaborative classification of hyperspectral images (HSI) with a complementary modality such as light detection and ranging (LiDAR) or synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which is known as multi-source remote sensing image classification (MRSIC), can combine rich spectral information with structural cues and is helpful for the recognition of complex ground objects. However, effectively incorporating these structural cues into multi-level spectral-spatial features and modeling their spatial relationships remain challenging under limited training samples. To address these problems, a multi-level convolutional collaborative classification network based on the DefMamba fusion mechanism (DMFNet) is proposed in this paper. First, monogenic phase congruency (MPC) responses are added to the complementary modality to enhance its structural information. Then, a dual-branch feature extraction module is constructed to derive multi-level features from HSI and the enhanced complementary modality and aggregate them into a joint representation. Finally, a DefMamba fusion module applies deformable selective scanning to the aggregated features, so as to adaptively model spatial dependencies according to the fused content. Experiments on three public multimodal remote sensing datasets, covering both HSI–LiDAR and HSI–SAR settings, demonstrate that DMFNet achieves the highest mean overall accuracy among the compared methods with 10 labeled training samples per class, with the largest improvement on the HSI-SAR scene. Additional experiments on Houston 2018 further evaluate its classification performance on a large-scale scene.

nodes.name: Cross-Dataset Generalization of Deep Learning for Retinal Vessel Segmentation in Fundus Images: External Evaluation from DRIVE to CHASE_DB1
nodes.venue: Bioengineering
nodes.abstract: Automated retinal vessel segmentation can support quantitative analysis of fundus photographs and facilitate measurement of vascular characteristics associated with ocular and systemic disease. Although deep-learning methods achieve high segmentation performance on benchmark datasets, their reliability may decrease when applied to images obtained under different acquisition conditions. This study evaluated the cross-dataset generalizability of a U-Net segmentation architecture incorporating an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet34 encoder. Sixteen images from the DRIVE dataset were used for model training and four were retained for in-domain validation. Images were resized to 256 × 256 pixels and processed using a consistent normalization pipeline, while spatial and photometric augmentation was applied during training. Without target-domain retraining or domain adaptation, the trained model was subsequently evaluated on the independent CHASE_DB1 dataset. Segmentation performance was assessed using the Dice coefficient, intersection over union (IoU), and sensitivity, together with qualitative examination of predicted vessel maps. On the held-out DRIVE images, the model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.7263, IoU of 0.5703, and sensitivity of 0.7201. On CHASE_DB1, performance decreased to 0.6269, 0.4573, and 0.5502, respectively. The disproportionately larger reduction in sensitivity indicated an increased frequency of missed vessel pixels under cross-dataset evaluation. Qualitative examination showed greater fragmentation and omission of fine and peripheral vascular structures in CHASE_DB1 images. These findings demonstrate that within-dataset performance may overestimate the robustness of retinal vessel segmentation models when transferred to a different imaging domain. External evaluation should therefore form an important component of retinal imaging artificial intelligence research. Future work should investigate higher-resolution processing, vessel-width-specific evaluation, multi-domain training, domain-adaptation strategies, and larger multicentre datasets to improve model generalizability.

nodes.name: Climate Resilience and Artificial Intelligence in Tourism: A Two-Stage Bibliometric Review and Post Hoc Evidence Audit (2019–2025)
nodes.venue: Sustainability
nodes.abstract: Background: Tourism is among the most climate-sensitive service industries, yet it is simultaneously undergoing rapid digital transformation through artificial intelligence (AI). The overlap and thematic relationships between the retrieved climate resilience and AI-in-tourism literature require empirical description. Methods: We conduct a PRISMA 2020- and PRISMA-S-informed, two-stage bibliometric science mapping review of Scopus and the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection (2019–2025), executed in 2026 and implemented in R (bibliometrix) under the SPAR-4-SLR protocol, complemented by a post hoc-focused full-text evidence audit developed during revision. Stage 1 maps the two parent literatures (N = 9513; Stream A = 2409, Stream B = 7177, shared = 73); Stage 2 is a separately searched exploratory corpus (N = 440) that is not the mathematical intersection of the parent streams. Key findings. The parent fields are large and expanding (24.59% annual growth) but show limited retrieved set overlap: cross-stream overlap is below 1% (0.64% unscreened; 0.77% screened; equivalently 3.03% of Stream A and 1.02% of Stream B), a measure of retrieved set overlap rather than of disciplinary isolation. The retained exploratory corpus has a 53.79% CAGR, and 214 of its 440 records fall outside the screened parent union. Its early relevance screening trail could not be reconstructed, so these findings describe the retained dataset and do not establish field-wide growth or convergence. Post hoc audit. Applying substantive tourism, AI, and climate hazard criteria to 100 assessed full texts identifies 14 studies for an exploratory audit (eight scenario-based, three prediction, and three association), spanning snow, thermal exposure, flooding and landslides, water, and recreation; none demonstrates an evaluated AI-led adaptation benefit. Implications: The findings motivate testing AI-supported climate risk decisions in tourism; they do not demonstrate improved resilience. Non-retrieval of 29 of 129 sought reports (22.5%) and post hoc selection limit the audit.

nodes.name: Beamforming generation via conditional variational autoencoder and adversarial learning
nodes.venue: International Journal of Microwave and Wireless Technologies
nodes.abstract: Abstract To address the limitations of current array antenna beamforming methods in terms of prediction accuracy and generalization capability, this paper proposes an efficient deep learning-based beamforming approach. The method first employs high-precision numerical computations in conjunction with an improved genetic algorithm to optimize the design and generate datasets that closely resemble practical scenarios, thereby providing a solid foundation for neural network training. On this basis, a generative model architecture combining a conditional variational autoencoder and a generative adversarial network is designed to enable accurate and efficient beamforming prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in planar array scenarios, with improved beam control accuracy compared to typical deep learning models, while significantly reducing computational complexity relative to conventional optimization algorithms.

nodes.name: International Journal of Microwave and Wireless Technologies
Artificial intelligence for ophthalmic vessel segmentation: from multimodal imaging to clinical translation
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Medicine
nodes.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based vessel segmentation converts color fundus photographs, scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO), optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), structural OCT, and anterior-segment images into quantitative vascular biomarkers. Strong performance within individual datasets has not consistently yielded reliable clinical measurements because errors can arise during acquisition, anatomical preprocessing, vessel extraction, biomarker calculation, and deployment. This structured narrative review compares segmentation tasks involving retinal vascular trees, OCTA capillary plexuses, the structural choroid and choriocapillaris, macular neovascularization, corneal neovascularization, and conjunctival microvasculature. We assess modern architectures in relation to vessel geometry, severe foreground-background imbalance, scale variation, crossings, and susceptibility to artifacts. The methods considered include multiscale feature pyramids, deformable and directional operators, Transformers, state-space models, diffusion approaches, and foundation models. We organize the synthesis around five evaluation levels: pixel overlap, centerline recovery, vascular topology, biomarker agreement, and clinical actionability. Public fundus and OCTA datasets are catalogued with their acquisition and annotation characteristics, and gaps in public anterior-segment vessel benchmarks are discussed. Because devices, data splits, labels, and post-processing differ substantially, reported metrics are summarized without ranking studies against one another. The review distinguishes structural OCT choroidal vascularity index from OCTA choriocapillaris flow-deficit mapping, as well as true vessel segmentation from global hyperemia grading. Clinical translation will require ocular-magnification correction, quality control of retinal layers and projection artifacts, external testing across devices and populations, out-of-distribution rejection, DICOM/PACS interoperability, prospective impact studies, and regulation as software as a medical device. We conclude that clinical utility depends on an auditable pipeline that measures structural error, biomarker uncertainty, and failure states throughout the workflow.

nodes.name: Application of radar remote sensing for cyclone damage mapping in Bangladesh: a coherence-based approach
nodes.venue: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
nodes.abstract: Rapid and reliable assessment of cyclone-induced damage remains a major challenge in coastal regions where cloud cover and limited accessibility constrain conventional approaches. This study presents a coherence-based Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) framework for identifying and quantifying cyclone-induced surface changes in the coastal districts of Bangladesh. Multi-temporal Sentinel-1 data were analyzed using interferometric coherence to capture spatial and temporal variations associated with five major cyclones: Amphan (2020), Sitrang (2022), Mocha (2023), Hamoon (2023), and Remal (2024). A time-series approach incorporating multiple pre-, during-, and post-event image pairs was implemented to distinguish cyclone-driven changes from natural surface variability and to improve detection reliability. The results reveal a consistent decline in coherence during cyclone events, followed by gradual recovery. Spatial analysis indicates that areas of significant coherence loss correspond to zones affected by flooding, vegetation damage, and structural disruption. Estimated damage extents varied across cyclones, with Remal (2024) showing the largest affected area (∼ 601 km 2 ), followed by Mocha (∼ 474 km 2 ), Amphan (∼ 288 km 2 ), Sitrang (∼ 122 km 2 ), and Hamoon (∼ 117 km 2 ). Validation using field observations and secondary data yielded an overall classification accuracy of 94 %, confirming the robustness of the coherence-based approach. Complementary inundation mapping further demonstrated that coherence captures a broader spectrum of cyclone impacts beyond flood extent alone, including wind-induced damage and geomorphic changes. This study establishes multi-temporal SAR coherence analysis as a scalable, cloud-independent, and operationally effective tool for rapid post-cyclone damage assessment. The proposed framework enhances the reliability of disaster monitoring in complex coastal environments and offers strong potential for integration into near-real-time disaster response systems. Future research should focus on integrating multi-sensor datasets and long-term coherence time series to refine damage characterization and reduce uncertainty.

nodes.name: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
An Adaptive Cloud Prediction Network for Supporting Space-Ground Laser Communication Links
nodes.venue: SAE Technical Paper Series
nodes.abstract: Space-ground laser communication links are highly susceptible to interruptions caused by cloud cover. Reliable dynamic scheduling of ground stations and seamless link handover, therefore, requires accurate short-term cloud-layer forecasts. However, cloud evolution is inherently chaotic, and atmospheric conditions exhibit evident seasonal non-stationarity. These factors weaken the prediction stability of existing models and make it difficult to maintain consistent accuracy over extended forecasting horizons. To address these challenges, this paper proposes KFMNet, an adaptive cloud prediction network that integrates Koopman theory with frequency-domain Mamba modeling. Unlike conventional frameworks that mainly process cloud features in the spatial domain, KFMNet embeds a linear state-space modeling mechanism into the frequency-domain feature evolution process. Specifically, an adaptive spectral gating mechanism is used to capture global cloud distribution patterns in the frequency domain, thereby reducing the computational burden associated with high-resolution image sequences. Meanwhile, a Koopman seasonal gating module introduces monthly prior knowledge into the network, enabling the model to adapt to atmospheric drift across seasonal transitions. Within the encoder-decoder backbone, KFMNet jointly incorporates temporal modeling, frequency-domain representation, and physical consistency constraints, providing a more stable framework for short-term cloud prediction. We evaluate KFMNet on multi-season cloud images collected over Nanjing and Beijing. The climate profiles of these two cities are markedly different. Under these conditions, KFMNet achieves competitive accuracy in cloud segmentation and shows a better ability to handle seasonal and regional shifts than several reference models. In essence, our method adapts well to changing atmospheric conditions and provides a new cloud prediction approach for space-ground laser link assurance. This method combines physical interpretability with the actual needs of real-world deployment.

nodes.name: Advancing Regional NO2 Estimation Using Machine Learning, TEMPO Satellite Data, and Geospatial Embeddings
nodes.venue: ACS ES&T Air
nodes.abstract: Abstract Ground-level air quality affects human health, well-being, and social outcomes. Gold-standard monitoring relies on calibrated, ground-based sensors that can be costly to install and maintain, limiting spatial coverage especially in resource-constrained regions that face higher pollution burdens. Recent advances in satellite remote sensing and machine learning offer a pathway to address these limitations by extending the spatial and temporal coverage of monitoring networks. However, models trained at national or global scales often exhibit substantial variability in regional performance, particularly in environments that are data-sparse or with heterogeneous emission sources. In this work, we investigate the benefits of developing a regional model for the American Gulf South. We develop an ensemble machine learning model that integrates satellite-derived NO2 retrievals with auxiliary data sets, including pretrained AlphaEarth location embeddings, to incorporate globally learned spatial representations into a regional framework. We show that these embeddings improve model performance and enable the most detailed estimates to date: ∼1 km × 1 km estimates of daily maximum NO2 across the Gulf South. These results demonstrate how combining regional modeling approaches with global foundation model representations can improve air quality estimation in complex environments, providing new information to support exposure assessment and decision-making in under-monitored communities.

nodes.name: A prototype algorithm for all-sky atmospheric temperature profile retrieval over ocean based on channel optimization for the FY-4M satellite
nodes.venue: Atmospheric Measurement Techniques
nodes.abstract: As the world's first geostationary satellite equipped with a passive microwave payload, China's FengYun-4M (FY-4M) is planned to be launched at the end of 2026, ushering in a new era of continuous observation of various geophysical parameters associated with weather processes. To better understand the observational characteristics of this satellite's more than a hundred channels, especially the potential application of its unique temperature hyperspectral channels (52.6–57.3 GHz) and several high-frequency channels (380 and 424 GHz) in the high-precision detection of atmospheric temperature profiles over ocean, this paper proposes a complete retrieval algorithm with a channel optimization scheme, based on information entropy theory and the Bayesian technique. Using degrees of freedom as an indicator, the ranking results of information contribution show that when hyperspectral channels are included, water vapor absorption channels and window channels used to obtain auxiliary information such as water vapor and hydrometeors are more important for the quantitative extraction of temperature profile information than traditional oxygen absorption channels at 50 and 118 GHz. Based on this, a corresponding channel configuration was constructed for all-weather temperature profile retrieval. The results of retrieval experiments show that the root mean square error (RMSE) remains below 0.5 K under clear-sky and cloudy conditions, and is within 0.8 K during precipitation. Additionally, the computational time is reduced by 14 % relative to the full-channel configuration. This suggests that the presented algorithm with this channel configuration scheme is able to achieve a favorable balance between retrieval accuracy and computational efficiency, making it a preferred choice for future operational retrieval systems.

nodes.name: A Hybrid Segmentation-Classification Framework for ECG Beat Recognition Using U‑Net and ResNet
nodes.venue: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis is a key step in many clinical tasks, because the ECG is the most commonly used non-invasive examination for assessing cardiac condition. State-of-the-art algorithms rely on digital signal processing (DSP) techniques, which require considerable effort to re-tune rules for new morphologies. In contrast, deep learning (DL) algorithms, especially for classification, are attracting growing attention in academia and industry. This study proposes a three-stage hierarchical deep learning framework. In Stage 1, a one-dimensional U-Net performs coarse segmentation of the ECG signal to separate background from regions of cardiac activity. In Stage 2, an attention-fusion U-Net takes the probability map produced in Stage 1 to localize and classify the P wave, QRS complex and T wave more precisely in time. In Stage 3, complete heartbeat segments are extracted from the Stage 2 segmentation result and a beat-level classification model is trained to classify beats, following the AAMI EC57 standard, into normal beats (N) and three classes of abnormal rhythm (S, V and Q). The Stage 1 and Stage 2 segmentation models achieved Macro F1 scores of 0.965 and 0.999, respectively, indicating very high waveform localization accuracy. Combined with soft max post-processing, the final four-class beat classifier reached a Macro F1 of 0.9779 and an overall accuracy of 0.9970 on the test set, and remained stable on the minority classes (V and Q).

nodes.name: Indian Journal of Computer Science and Technology
A 3D Vision-Based Localization Method for Automated Loading of Large-Sized Heat Exchangers
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: Manual loading of large-sized finned-tube heat exchangers has low productivity and imposes substantial physical demands on workers. In addition, industrial 3D vision systems often produce large regions of missing depth data when imaging highly reflective metallic surfaces, which complicates grasp-pose estimation for robot manipulators. Unlike randomly sparse measurements, these reflection-induced depth failures are spatially continuous and view-dependent: specular reflection may redirect the projected signal away from the receiver, producing invalid or erroneous depth values over substantial surface regions. Under such conditions, depth-completion methods may generate geometrically plausible but unverified estimates in unobserved regions, whereas correspondence-based registration becomes unreliable when valid overlap, stable local geometry, and distinctive features are simultaneously reduced. This paper develops a model-specific 3D vision-based localization method for automated loading of large-sized heat exchangers affected by structured reflection-induced point-cloud incompleteness. First, an industrial 3D camera synchronously acquires color and depth images. A hybrid interlayer-cardboard extraction strategy uses two-dimensional (2D) color-threshold morphological segmentation and three-dimensional (3D) back-projection as the primary branch, while activating a geometry-based point-cloud fallback when the color-based branch produces no valid candidate or returns a component count inconsistent with the production-task configuration. In 129 paired RGB and point-cloud samples, the color-based branch correctly processed 122 samples, and the fallback recovered the remaining seven cases under the evaluated production-line conditions. For product localization, the method integrates three complementary geometric operations: projected-area minimization for yaw estimation and lateral alignment, tail-feature constraints for head–tail determination and longitudinal anchoring, and inverse mapping of the complete CAD template to the observed product pose. This coordinated procedure exploits the remaining reliable global and regional geometry without reconstructing the missing surface, thereby reducing the pose-estimation bias caused by the shifted centroid of the incomplete point cloud. In the main registration experiment, the method was evaluated using 436 production-line samples with different stacking poses and levels of missing data, including severe cases with a missing rate greater than 30%. This 436-sample evaluation yielded an overall mean translation error of 5.21 mm, a nearest-neighbor RMSE of 1.98 mm, and an average registration-operator runtime of 531.03 ms per registration. By exploiting known product geometry and a reflection-resistant tail feature rather than relying on completed depth values, the proposed method provides deterministic localization for the evaluated heat-exchanger models and production-line conditions.

nodes.name: Data-Faithful Natural Language Generation for Explaining Fitness-Market Anomalies
nodes.venue: Anais do XVII Simpósio Brasileiro de Tecnologia da Informação e da Linguagem Humana (STIL 2026)
nodes.abstract: This study presents an integrated pipeline that transforms anomaly-detection outputs from global fitness-market data into data-faithful narratives. Using a 132-country panel and a 2019 baseline, we analyze observed post-COVID-19 recovery through 2025, while treating 2026 only as a modelled extension. Four complementary detectors—regional-median deviations, linear-regression residuals, Random Forest residuals, and Isolation Forest—are combined through method agreement and mapped to a rule-based typology. A deterministic, template-based Natural Language Generation (NLG) component then produces short, medium, and complete explanations from tabular evidence. In 2025, 14 countries were consensus anomalies; Guyana exemplified market growth without participatory expansion, with revenue recovery of +401.43%, participation recovery of -2.06%, and a 403.50-point gap. All 132 narratives passed automatic factual-consistency checks. These checks validate field preservation rather than fluency, usefulness, or explanatory quality; human evaluation remains future work.

STLFM-based integration of sensing and secure communication in optical fiber
nodes.venue: Optics Express
nodes.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication in optical fiber (ISAC-OF) provides a promising solution for innovative applications such as smart cities, intelligent transportation, and ocean monitoring. However, dedicated sensing waveforms may increase the observability of optical links and introduce additional physical-layer security risks. In this paper, we propose and experimentally demonstrate an integrated sensing and secure communication scheme for optical fiber links. Quantum noise stream cipher (QNSC) is used to protect the confidentiality of payload symbols, while a symmetric triangular linear frequency modulation (STLFM) waveform is reused as a training sequence for communication and as a probing waveform for distributed sensing. QNSC inherently introduces a transmission penalty due to ciphertext constellation expansion. Compared with a repeated-QPSK training sequence reference, STLFM provides more accurate and stable frame-start estimation and more effective frequency offset compensation (FOC), thereby reducing receiver impairments and improving signal recovery. In a 200 Gbit/s, 100 km simulation, the proposed scheme achieves a received-power gain of 1.49 dB at the 7% HD-FEC threshold compared with a repeated-QPSK training sequence reference. In a 10 Gbit/s, 10.1 km proof-of-concept experiment, a received-power gain of 1 dB is obtained under the same threshold. The eavesdropper bit error rate (BER), together with the number of masked signals (NMS) and detection failure probability (DFP) evaluations, indicates that quantum noise masking increases ciphertext-state ambiguity and enhances payload confidentiality. For sensing, the scheme reconstructs distributed vibration signals along the 10.1 km fiber and achieves a spatial resolution of 3.9 m and a strain resolution of 22.37 n ε / H z . These results show that secure communication and distributed vibration sensing can be jointly realized over the same fiber link, while the shared STLFM waveform improves signal recovery.

nodes.name: Synergistic Use of Multitemporal SAR and Optical Data with Random Forest Approach for Rice Mapping in Bangladesh
nodes.abstract: Accurate in-season crop mapping is vital for national food security, yet traditional ground-based estimation methods in Bangladesh often lack precision. This study develops a robust machine-learning framework to map Boro rice in the Manikganj district by integrating Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Sentinel-2 optical imagery. To overcome the challenge of seasonal cloud cover, Sentinel-1 VH polarization was utilized to identify unique backscatter reductions during the transplantation phase (late February to early March) caused by specular reflection from flooded fields. By combining these SAR signatures with high-resolution spectral indices (NDVI, EVI, and BSI) from Sentinel-2 during peak growth stages, the research captures the distinct phenological signatures of paddy rice. A pixel-based Random Forest algorithm was applied within the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform, utilizing about 200 field-verified reference points per sub-district (1,385 in total) for training and validation. The results demonstrated high classification performance, with overall accuracies ranging from 88.1% to 94.9% across the seven sub-districts. Furthermore, a comparison with official government statistics revealed a minimal total area difference of only 2.34%, underscoring the reliability of this integrated satellite approach for operational crop monitoring.

nodes.name: MAPPING FORENSIC ACCOUNTING’S SCHOLARLY LANDSCAPE IN NIGERIA: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF FRAUD DETECTION AND PREVENTION RESEARCH
nodes.venue: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
nodes.abstract: Nigeria’s persistent exposure to financial fraud and systemic corruption has intensified the demand for robust investigative tools, with forensic accounting emerging as a critical mechanism for enhancing transparency, accountability, and institutional integrity. Despite its theoretical promise, the scholarly engagement with forensic accounting in Nigeria remains fragmented and underdeveloped. This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of 138 peer-reviewed articles published between 2017 and 2025, retrieved exclusively from the Scopus database, to examine the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and research gaps in forensic accounting and fraud-related scholarship. Using the Bibliometrix package in RStudio, the study maps publication trends, identifies prolific authors and institutions, visualises co-authorship networks, and explores keyword co-occurrence and thematic clusters. The findings reveal a steady growth in scholarly output, with international collaboration moderately present but Nigerian contributions notably sparse despite the country’s high corruption index. Dominant themes include fraud detection, forensic audit techniques, and data analytics, while emerging areas such as blockchain, smart contracts, and AI-driven fraud prevention remain underexplored. This study underscores the need for context-specific frameworks, interdisciplinary collaboration, and strategic investment in Nigeria's forensic accounting education and research infrastructure. This can be achieved by illuminating the structural dynamics and intellectual gaps within the field. This study offers actionable insights for scholars, policymakers, and anti-graft institutions seeking to leverage forensic accounting to combat financial crime.

nodes.name: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
Geospatial Assessment of Land Use and Land Cover Change Impacts on Wetland Ecosystem Services in West Arsi Zone, Ethiopia
nodes.abstract: Human livelihoods and well-being rely heavily on ecosystem services (ESs) provided by natural environments, with wetlands standing out as some of the most biologically diverse and economically valuable ecosystems worldwide. Despite their importance, wetlands face increasing threats from land use and land cover (LULC) changes driven by human activities. This study examines how LULC changes have affected wetland ecosystem service values (ESVs) in the West Arsi Zone of Oromia, Ethiopia, over a 30-year period from 1995 to 2025. Multi-temporal Landsat images were analyzed using cloud-based geospatial tools on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform, and land cover classification was done with the Random Forest (RF) machine-learning algorithm. Field observations and ground reference data helped improve classification accuracy and identify the main drivers behind land cover changes. Ecosystem service values were estimated using a locally adapted benefit transfer method based on established valuation coefficients. The results show that rapid population growth, agricultural expansion, urban development, and infrastructure construction are the key forces driving LULC changes in the area. Settlement expansion significantly increased cropland-related ESVs from around USD 0.1 million to USD 2.5 million. However, this economic gain came mostly at the cost of wetlands, whose ecosystem service values dropped sharply from USD 1.17 million to just USD 0.05 million. Overall, the total ecosystem service value of the landscape fell by 3.9%, from USD 16.55 million in 1995 to USD 15.91 million in 2025. These findings highlight clear biodiversity loss and declining ecosystem function, emphasizing the urgent need for sustainable land-use planning that balances socio-economic growth with wetland conservation to protect long-term ecological health and human well-being.

nodes.name: GenAI-Powered Smart Traffic Assistant: A Multimodal AI Framework for Real-Time Traffic Prediction, Route Recommendation, and Explainable Urban Mobility
nodes.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
nodes.abstract: Urban traffic management increasingly requires systems that can reason over heterogeneous, time-varying information rather than rely only on static maps or historical averages. This paper presents the GenAI-Powered Smart Traffic Assistant, a prototype intelligent transportation platform that combines real-time location, traffic and weather inputs, historical traffic data, machine-learning-based congestion prediction, computer-vision vehicle detection, route recommendation, alerts, explainable AI (XAI), and role-aware dashboards in a unified workflow. The system is derived from a semester project report and its associated prototype deployment. The design follows a layered client-server architecture with a web/mobile oriented interface, application services, machine-learning components, and persistent traffic data. A structured development methodology is used to integrate data collection, preprocessing, prediction, recommendation, visualization, security, and maintenance. Rather than claiming benchmark accuracy that is not reported in the source project, the paper evaluates the prototype through functional coverage, architecture consistency, safety constraints, and explicit non-functional targets. The resulting framework provides a practical foundation for multimodal traffic assistance and a pathway toward live CCTV integration, IoT sensing, adaptive signal control, continuous model learning, and smart-city interoperability.

nodes.name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
Evaluation of the EarthCARE aerosol classification scheme using ACTRIS/EARLINET observations.
nodes.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
nodes.abstract: Aerosol typing plays an important role in identifying aerosol sources, monitoring environmental events, and mitigating impacts. Understanding the origin and characteristics of aerosols is essential to detect aerosol hazards, issue early warnings and minimize their potential impact on climate, air quality, and public health. To date, several aerosol typing schemes have been developed within ACTRIS (Aerosol, Clouds and Trace Gases Research Infrastructure) and EARLINET (European Aerosol Research Lidar Network; data.earlinet.org) and provide the predominant aerosol type or aerosol mixture in the atmospheric column [1-5]. Similarly, aerosol classification from space lidars offers global coverage and can either be used complementary in retrievals or radiative-closure assessments. The ESA-JAXA EarthCARE satellite mission, launched in May 2024, provides vertical profiles of aerosols, clouds, and precipitation properties, along with radiative fluxes. Equipped with a high spectral resolution ATmospheric LIDar (ATLID), a Doppler Cloud Profiling Radar (CPR), a MultiSpectral Imager (MSI), and a BroadBand Radiometer (BBR), EarthCARE is designed to advance aerosol characterization via synergistic usage of the aforementioned sensors. As a High Spectral Resolution Lidar (HSRL), ATLID provides a feature mask based solely on aerosol-intensive properties, without relying on assumptions, as CALIPSO. Many EARLINET stations are actively measuring during EarthCARE overpasses when the satellite’s footprint lies within a 100 km radius from the ground station, making correlative measurements from August 2024 to present. Ground based measurements from ACTRIS/ EARLINET ([6]; data.earlinet.org) include particle backscatter coefficient, particle extinction coefficient, and particle depolarization ratio profiles. The ACTRIS/EARLINET database has been used for developing aerosol typing algorithms based on type-dependent intensive optical properties [1-5]. The most common intensive optical parameters used for aerosol-typing are the lidar ratio, the particle depolarization ratio, and the Ångström exponent (or Color ratio). Depending on the availability of the particle linear depolarization ratio and the quality of the provided lidar profiles, the derived typing within EARLINET can be either of high or low resolution. In the high-resolution typing of NATALI classification for example, 14 aerosol types can be distinguished (i.e., Continental, ContinentalPolluted, Dust, Maritime/CC, Smoke, Volcanic, Coastal, CoastalPolluted, ContinentalDust, ContinentalSmoke, DustPolluted, MaritimeMineral, MixedDust and MixedSmoke). In the low-resolution typing, five predominant aerosol types can be provided (i.e., Dust, ContinentalPolluted, Smoke, Continental, and Maritime), either pure or mixed. EarthCARE, which is a 355-nm lidar, makes use of two intensive properties: the particle depolarization ratio and particle lidar ratio (L2 products) to assign an aerosol type [7]. EarthCARE’s ATLID classification scheme defines ten aerosol types, with classification made at two resolution levels: low and medium. The typing is based on the size, composition, and optical characteristics of the observed aerosols. The types are as follows: Dust, Sea_salt, Continental_Pollution, Smoke, Dusty_smoke, Dusty_mix, Stratospheric_Ash, Stratospheric_Sulfate, Stratospheric_Smoke, Unknown (Aerosol Target has a very low probability (no class assigned)). Therefore, EarthCARE’s aerosol classification assessment requires comparison with ACTRIS/EARLINET classification schemes. In this study we selected cases with various atmospheric conditions to evaluate the EarthCARE aerosol classification scheme by assessing its performance through ACTRIS/EARLINET profiles and the predominant aerosol types identified by the different network’s algorithms. The ground-based observations from the following 12 stations are included in this evaluation: Antikythera (AKY), Potenza (POT), Leipzig (LEI), Bucharest (INO), Cabauw (CBW), Thessaloniki (THE), Granada (GRA), La Reunion (RUN), Clermont-Ferrand (PUY), Barcelona (BRC), Cyprus CAO Nicosia (NCS), Kuopio (KUO). These stations cover a diverse range of aerosol conditions, including dust-dominated regions (e.g., NCS, GRA), urban/industrial sites (e.g., BRC, POT, CBW), marine environments (e.g., RUN) and mixed or background sites (e.g., AKY, KUO). In total 283 measurements have been performed during EarthCARE overpasses above these stations. In the following, we consider only the collocated measurements related to overpasses within a 100 km radius from the station, and time differences within 1.5 hours are used to ensure the aerosol homogeneity. Also, we ensure that both the ground-based station and the satellite observed the same air masses. Last, we will take into account cases with distances over 100 km during intense aerosol episodes such as desert dust intrusions. The EarthCARE lidar aerosol profile processor (A-PRO; [8]): the A-AER, A-EBD, A-TC, mainly from AC and AD baselines, and L1 and L2 nighttime EARLINET quality-assured measurements are used for the aerosol classification evaluation.

nodes.name: Comment on essd-2026-495
nodes.abstract: Abstract. The advent of big data in Earth observation, coupled with recent advances in Artificial Intelligence, has led to the development of geospatial embeddings. These compact, information-rich feature vectors are designed for direct use in machine learning (ML) applications across a wide range of downstream tasks, such as forest monitoring. Motivated by the limitations of existing global forest products and policy requirements like the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), we (1) evaluate whether lightweight classifiers applied to satellite embeddings from the Google DeepMind Alpha Earth Foundation (AEF) can accurately map global forest and tree crop extents, and (2) we introduce the resulting GEM-Forest dataset. GEM-Forest is a global satellite embedding–based dataset at 10 m spatial resolution for 2020 that provides a consistent classification across three classes: forest, non-forest, and tree crops. Our comparison of multiple ML approaches ranging from linear models to neural networks showed similar performance across classifiers, while linear models often outperformed more complex models. This consistency indicates that the embeddings encode highly informative and linearly separable structures for global forest discrimination, which includes tree crop separation. Based on these findings, a linear Support Vector Machine was used to generate the final GEM-Forest dataset, which outperformed eight existing global forest, tree cover, or land cover maps on two global validation datasets, while it placed second on the JRC’s global forest validation dataset. Across all three datasets, the forest class achieved omission errors of 12–18 % and commission errors of 16–21 %, with overall accuracies from 88 % to 92 %. Misclassifications of tree crops as forests varied between 0.5 % and 14.8 %, with a producer’s accuracy above 85 % for most tree crop datasets, whereas the classification of European tree crops remains the most challenging. Globally, GEM-Forest maps 3,919 million hectares (Mha) of forest for 2020, representing a 5.9 % underestimation relative to FAO reports. This variance is partly attributed to the exclusion of unstocked forest areas from our forest definition, discrepancies in country-based forest definitions, and misclassification errors that occurred primarily within open forests and forest–shrubland transition zones. Overall, these results demonstrate that satellite embeddings combined with simple ML approaches support highly accurate, computationally efficient global forest and tree crop mapping. The open-access release of the GEM-Forest dataset and its ML model weights (both available in Paluba et al., 2026; DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18921586) can support international policy decisions and allows direct and straightforward temporal transferability for other years.

nodes.name: Same computation, different scenes: a single-site comparison of Sentinel-2 L2A composites from Google Earth Engine and Microsoft Planetary Computer
nodes.abstract: Google Earth Engine (GEE) and Microsoft Planetary Computer (MPC) distribute Sentinel-2 Level-2A surface reflectance, and their outputs can be combined in one time series. Over a 73 ha cattle farm in northern Colombia, we tested whether the two platforms yield the same parcel-scale vegetation and water indices and, where they differ, whether the difference originates in the product (the L2A scene), the processing chain (masking, 3 × 3 smoothing, NDVI, EVI, NDWI and monthly median) or the scene universe (which acquisitions enter a composite). For the ten pairs in which both platforms served the same product, scene classification and harmonised reflectance matched in every comparable pixel, and the same chain run locally or server-side in GEE agreed within 10⁻⁶. The catalogues, however, did not hold the same scenes. Between June 2024 and April 2025, 10 of 146 scene–tile records existed only in GEE, six of them Sentinel-2C records from around the satellite's entry into operations, and none only in MPC. In 22 of 136 common records, all from June–July 2024, the catalogues held different L2A generations; of the ten such pairs with valid pixels, one had a different cloud mask. Adding the GEE-only scenes shifted mean monthly NDVI over the farm by −0.0005 (December 2024) and −0.0087 (January 2025), and by up to −0.028 in a public 1 km² demonstration area (January 2025). For the operations tested, the platforms are computationally equivalent, but combining them requires reconciling scene inventories. The reconciliation table, composite scene lists and open-source tools are released.
